title: Влияние магнитного поля на сверхзвуковые флаттерные колебания прямоугольной пластинки, помещенной в температурное поле
journal: Mechanics - Proceedings of National Academy of Sciences of Armenia
abstract: The nature of nonlinear oscillations of an isotropic rectangular plate in a supersonic gas flow in the presence of both thermal and magnetic fields is studied. The study was carried out taking into account two types of nonlinearity: aerodynamic (quadratic and cubic) and geometric (cubic). It was established that due to aerodynamic nonlinearity, the relation A(ν) (where A is the amplitude of nonlinear oscillations, ν is the parameter characterizing the velocity of the flowing gas) is a multivalued function in certain ranges of velocity ν. This fact is depicted in the graphs presented in the text in the form of different branches. In these figures, the lower branches are most likely unstable. The existence of such ranges of variation of v is shown, where flutter-type oscillations cannot be excited. The combined effect of thermal and magnetic fields on the behavior of nonlinear oscillations is studied.

title: VOICES OF RESILIENCE: LOCAL FLOOD MANAGEMENT PRACTICES IN BARANGAY BANQUERO, REINA MERCEDES, ISABELA
journal: EPRA International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research (IJMR)
abstract: This study explores the lived experiences and grassroots flood management practices of residents in Barangay Banquero, Reina Mercedes, Isabela—a high-risk rural community situated along the floodplains of the Cagayan River basin. While formal disaster frameworks rely heavily on top-down institutional mandates, this research examines the localized, human dimension of survival and community-driven resilience. Utilizing a qualitative phenomenological design, semi-structured interviews were conducted with fifteen long-term residents who have extensive histories of navigating severe flooding events. Through thematic analysis, the study reveals a sophisticated repertoire of self-reliant coping strategies, most notably the practice of "vertical displacement"—the multi-stage modification of household structures using makeshift lofts and elevated platforms to safeguard material assets. These practices are deeply sustained by kinship-based logistics and informal social networks that dictate organic evacuation movements. However, the findings reveal a critical "preparedness ceiling," indicating that the escalating intensity of climate-driven typhoons has surpassed a threshold where personal preparation yields diminishing returns. This mismatch inflicts a recurring psychosomatic burden on residents, characterized by anticipatory panic and physical exhaustion. Ultimately, these insights highlight the urgent need for local disaster management policies to shift away from standardized relief and instead integrate, support, and institutionalize these organic grassroots strategies to build genuine community resilience.

title: Tree Stem Perimeter Estimation for Forestry Robots via Residual Learning and LiDAR–RGB Fusion
abstract: Accurate estimation of tree stem perimeter is essential for robotic forest mapping and inventory applications. While light detection and ranging (LiDAR)–camera fusion enables automated stem detection and geometric reconstruction, perimeter estimates derived from partial LiDAR observations exhibit systematic bias due to occlusions, limited angular coverage, and violations of ideal cylindrical assumptions. These effects introduce systematic errors that cannot be fully resolved by geometric reconstruction or temporal smoothing alone. This paper proposes a residual learning framework that enhances geometric perimeter estimation by learning a data-driven correction term while preserving the interpretability of the underlying model. A mobile robot equipped with a three-dimensional LiDAR and an RGB camera collects synchronized data in forest environments. Tree stems are detected in RGB images and associated with LiDAR points through calibrated projection. A geometric baseline perimeter is computed by fitting a circular model to a diameter-at-breast-height cross-section extracted from incomplete LiDAR observations. A shallow multilayer perceptron then predicts the residual between the geometric estimate and manually measured ground-truth perimeter using observation-derived features. Filtering improves stability but does not remove systematic bias, whereas residual learning achieves consistent bias correction. Experimental results demonstrate reductions exceeding 40% in both mean absolute and root mean squared errors, together with a substantial improvement in the coefficient of determination from 0.48 to 0.86. Error distributions become more centered and consistent across varying sensing distances and stem sizes, confirming robust generalization to unseen trees. The proposed method operates as a lightweight post-processing module, making it suitable for real-time deployment on mobile forestry robots.

title: School-Enterprise Cooperation and Vocational Safety Literacy Formation: A Structural Equation Modeling Approach in Chinese Higher Vocational Colleges
abstract: School-enterprise cooperation (SEC) is a central pillar of Chinese vocational education policy, yet how its specific dimensions affect students’ safety literacy remains empirically underexamined. This study disaggregates SEC into three dimensions: co-developed curriculum, enterprise practicum participation, and enterprise mentor guidance. Based on Theory of Planned Behavior, the mediation chain path of safety cognition→safety attitude→safety behavioral intention is examined to investigate the effect of three dimensions of SEC on vocational safety literacy. A total of 327 higher vocational students are surveyed in a district in Guangdong Province. Bootstrap mediation tests and structural equation modeling are used for statistical analysis. Results Enterprise practicum (β=0.31, p<0.001), guidance model (β=0.19, p<0.01) and co-developed curriculum (β=0.11, p<0.05), have the biggest direct effect (β) in chain mediation, with the first half “attitude to intention” (β=0.29) reaching significance. As the “last link of the chain”, practicum based experiential engagement may be need more to be emphasized rather than the curriculum reform alone, so does formalize safety mentorship.

title: Rostral lesion shift and tract-specific degeneration drive functional heterogeneity in degenerative cervical myelopathy
Reframing Zoonotic Spillover: Deforestation, Biodiversity Loss, and Climate Change as Molecular Epidemiological Risk Multipliers
journal: Journal of Environment, Climate, and Ecology
abstract: This review argues that deforestation, biodiversity loss, and climate change must be redefined as measurable molecular epidemiological risk multipliers for zoonotic spillover, rather than merely background conditions. These interacting drivers have a direct effect on epidemiologically significant parameters like core density, genetic diversity of the virus, contact with the interface, and the capacity of the vectors. First, forest fragmentation and deforestation generate edge effects that cause reservoir species to move into human-altered landscapes and increase the vulnerability to pathogens such as Ebola and Nipah. Second, the loss of biodiversity due to disturbance caused by extra species also alters the composition of communities towards more competitive reservoir species, theoretically, residents of a protective dilution effect. Third, climate change increases viral replication in response to temperature and expands the geographic distribution of arthropod vectors, increasing the transmission of diseases like dengue and Lyme. The association of such macro-environmental transformations with the size-scale phenomena makes this manuscript illustrate how anthropogenic forces shape the biosphere structure to be disease-favourable. We come to the conclusion that reactive pathogen surveillance should not be used as an effective means of protecting against pandemics anymore. Rather, it requires a shift of paradigm where proactive forest protection, biodiversity protection and climate mitigation all become part of the working heart of One Health systems.
